newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia extends cellphone rights till 2014 - papers.
newsitem.headline: Colombia extends cellphone rights till 2014 - papers.

text.p: Colombia has agreed to extend the concessions of six cellular telephone companies operating across the country until the year 2014 in exchange for a total payment of $130 million, local news reports said Friday.
The concessions were orginally set to expire in 2004 but Communications Minister Saulo Arboleda signed a new contract Thursday granting the 10-year extension, the reports said.
In exchange, the six companies agreed to pay the government a total of $100 million before June 30, and an additional $30 million prior to Nov. 30, Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper said.

It quoted Arboleda as saying longer operating contracts would ensure that Colombia's cellular phone companies have greater access to long-term credits to finance expansion plans in a market that opened just three years ago and still has enormous potential for growth.
The companies benefitting from longer operating rights are Comcel, Celumovil, Occel, Cocelco, Celcaribe and a subsidiary of Celumovil that operates along the Caribbean coast.
